requirements.title: Input and output statements define reading, writing, and optional editing
requirements.definition: Input statements transfer data from external media or internal files to internal storage and are called reading; output statements transfer data from internal storage to external media or internal files and are called writing; some input/output statements specify editing.

pending.input-reading-transfer: Use a future internal READ from a nonblank character record into an integer initialized to -777; expect IOSTAT zero and the integer changed to the record value, proving input transfer rather than default state.
pending.output-writing-transfer: Use a future internal WRITE to a character variable prefilled with nonblank sentinel characters; expect IOSTAT zero and exact transferred characters, proving output transfer to an internal file.
pending.editing-specified-by-some-io-statements: Compare a formatted internal WRITE using an explicit format with an unformatted or list-directed control only after those forms are registered; assert only the exact characters fixed by the format, not processor-dependent external formatting.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. requirements.title: Auxiliary input/output statements manipulate or inquire about an external medium
requirements.definition: Besides data-transfer statements, auxiliary input/output statements manipulate the external medium or describe/inquire about properties of a connection to it.

pending.auxiliary-manipulates-external-medium: After OPEN/CLOSE/REWIND/INQUIRE are registered, create a known scratch or named file and use an auxiliary statement such as REWIND before reading known records; assert only portable success and data order.
pending.auxiliary-inquires-connection-properties: After INQUIRE is registered, open a known unit and inquire an established property such as OPENED into a logical initialized to .true. or .false. opposite the expected value; assert the property changes to the portable expected value.

requirements.title: The Fortran input/output statements are the listed statement forms
requirements.definition: The input/output statement set is BACKSPACE, CLOSE, ENDFILE, FLUSH, INQUIRE, OPEN, PRINT, READ, REWIND, WAIT, and WRITE.

pending.listed-io-statement-set: Source-use inventory plan: future statement catalogues for each listed statement cross-reference this unit; no single-image execution can prove the statement set is exhaustive without relying on parser diagnostics owned by each statement syntax rule.

requirements.title: Files are record files or stream files by composition
requirements.definition: A file is composed of either file storage units or records; record files are composed of records and stream files are composed of file storage units.

pending.file-storage-unit-composition: Use future unformatted stream access to write a known scalar sequence and inquire POS before and after; assert only monotonic portable position properties named by stream rules, not byte counts.
pending.record-file-composition: Use future sequential formatted access to write two known records and read them back in order with nondefault sentinels.
pending.stream-file-composition: Use future stream access with POS= to read a previously written position; assert only data recovery from an identified position, not storage-unit size.

requirements.title: A processor may expose both record and stream views with processor-dependent correspondence
requirements.definition: A processor may allow the same file to be viewed both as a record file and as a stream file; if so, the relationship between stream file storage units and record-file records is processor dependent.

pending.dual-record-stream-view-permitted: No portable oracle requires that a processor provide both views for a particular external medium; a future profile may document support but must not make it a conformance expectation.
pending.record-stream-correspondence-processor-d: No portable oracle may require a specific mapping between record boundaries and stream positions; future tests must obtain positions through POS= inquiry and avoid comparing to byte counts or newline encodings.

requirements.title: Files are classified as external or internal
requirements.definition: A file is either an external file or an internal file.

pending.external-or-internal-file-classification: Use one future external-file data transfer through an OPENed unit and one internal-file data transfer through a CHARACTER variable; assert the respective portable data effects, not any implementation representation.

Defines the auxiliary input/output statement role.
Mixed file-composition definitions and processor latitude are split into fine units.
Processor permission and processor-dependent mapping; no fixed mapping is required.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clause 12 (batch145), the clause's first packet. Every base and fine unit classified and hash-verified against the pinned J3/24-007 census by an independent fresh-context reviewer who read the original pages 242-246 and confirmed 12.3.3.4 ends before 12.3.4.1. Mixed obligation/latitude units were swept in both directions and all splits recorded; no unit left unresolved; no numbered R/C rule in scope; no requirement based on a NOTE; no no-portable-oracle claim found to be over-suppression and no pending plan found vacuous. Source accounting only: no fixture, compiler invocation or execution credit.
